"'''Hello'''" is a song by American singer and songwriter [[Lionel Richie]]. Taken as the third single from his second solo album, ''[[Can't Slow Down (Lionel Richie album)|Can't Slow Down]]'' (1983), the song was released in 1984 and reached number one on three ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' music charts: the [[Billboard Hot 100|pop chart]] (for two weeks), the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|R&B chart]] (for three weeks),<ref>{{cite book |title=Top R&B/Hip-Hop Singles: 1942-2004 |last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=492}}</ref> and the [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary chart]] (for six weeks). The song also went to number one on the [[UK Singles Chart]] for six weeks.<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums">{{cite book | first=David |last=Roberts |year=2006 |title=British Hit Singles & Albums |title-link=Guinness World Records#The Guinness Book of British Hit Singles |edition=19th |publisher=[[Guinness World Records]] |location=London |isbn=1-904994-10-5 |pages=434–5}}</ref>

The song was subject to a lawsuit by songwriter Marjorie Hoffman White, who accused Richie of plagiarizing her 1978 composition "I'm Not Ready to Go".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.upi.com/Archives/1984/07/04/A-Long-Island-song-writer-has-filed-a-1/4560457761600/ |title=A Long Island song writer has filed a $1... |work=[[United Press International]] |date=July 4, 1984 |access-date=June 16, 2024 |location=New York |archive-date=December 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241218023342/https://www.upi.com/Archives/1984/07/04/A-Long-Island-song-writer-has-filed-a-1/4560457761600/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

"Hello" is a song by American singer and songwriter Lionel Richie. Taken as the third single from his second solo album, Can't Slow Down (1983), the song was released in 1984 and reached number one on three Billboard music charts: the pop chart (for two weeks), the R&B chart (for three weeks), and the Adult Contemporary chart (for six weeks). The song also went to number one on the UK Singles Chart for six weeks.

The song was subject to a lawsuit by songwriter Marjorie Hoffman White, who accused Richie of plagiarizing her 1978 composition "I'm Not Ready to Go".

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext: ''[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cashbox]]'' said that the song "is as melodic and heartwrenching as anything [Richie] has done previously and that’s saying something."<ref name=cb>{{cite magazine |title=Reviews |magazine=[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cashbox]] |url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/80s/1984/CB-1984-02-25.pdf |date=February 25, 1984 |access-date=2022-07-22 |page=7 |archive-date=November 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127200514/https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/80s/1984/CB-1984-02-25.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref>
sections.text: Cashbox said that the song "is as melodic and heartwrenching as anything [Richie] has done previously and that’s saying something."

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext:
The song is written in the key of [[A minor]]. The verses follow the [[chord progression]] of Am<sub>9</sub>—Cmaj<sub>7</sub>/G—Fmaj<sub>7</sub>—C<sub>6</sub>/G—Fmaj<sub>7</sub>. The chorus features a [[Neapolitan chord]] (Bb).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtdFPE.asp?ppn=MN0073920&ref=google |title=Lionel Richie "Hello" Sheet Music in A Minor (transposable) |date=March 21, 2011 |website=Musicnotes.com |access-date=March 29, 2014}}</ref>

The composition began with the line, "Hello, is it me you're looking for?". After producer [[James Anthony Carmichael]] arrived at Richie's house for a songwriting session, Richie jokingly greeted him with the line, to which Carmichael replied, "Finish that song." Richie initially felt the idea was "corny", but ultimately, "by the time I finished the verse, I fell in love with the song again."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/entertainment/article/lionel-richie-recalls-early-distaste-for-hello-as-hit-song-turns-30/ |title=Lionel Richie recalls early distaste for 'Hello' as hit song turns 30 |last=Patch |first=Nick |work=[[CTV News]] |date=May 16, 2014}}</ref>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The [[music video]] for "Hello", directed by [[Bob Giraldi]], features the story of Richie as a theater and acting teacher having a seemingly unrequited love for a blind student (Laura Carrington). He discovers the feeling is mutual after he finds that she is sculpting a likeness of his head in clay.

Several publications have likened the song's theme and video to British singer [[Adele]]'s later song "[[Hello (Adele song)|Hello]]".<ref name=Horton>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/music/news/hello-is-it-me-youre-looking-for/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/music/news/hello-is-it-me-youre-looking-for/ |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Lionel Richie responds to Adele's 'Hello' |last=Horton |first=Helena |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=October 26, 2015 |access-date=October 27, 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.radiotimes.com/news/2015-10-26/hello-adele-is-it-lionel-richie-youre-looking-for |title=Lionel Richie responds on Instagram to Adele 'Hello' music video mash-up |last=Doran |first=Sarah |work=[[Radio Times]] |date=October 26, 2015 |access-date=October 28, 2015 |archive-date=July 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200722022919/https://www.radiotimes.com/news/2015-10-26/hello-adele-is-it-lionel-richie-youre-looking-for/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

A [[UK garage]] cover by Jhay Palmer featuring MC Image reached No. 69 on the [[UK Singles Chart]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/11596/jhay-palmer-ft-mc-image/ |title=JHAY PALMER FEATURING MC IMAGE | full Official Chart History | Official Charts Company |website=[[Official Charts Company]] |access-date=August 5, 2021 |archive-date=April 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190405221923/https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/11596/jhay-palmer-ft-mc-image/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and No. 11 on the [[UK Dance Singles Chart]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/dance-singles-chart/20020421/104/ |title=Official Dance Singles Chart Top 40 | Official Charts Company |website=[[Official Charts Company]] |access-date=August 5, 2021 |archive-date=August 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805113836/https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/dance-singles-chart/20020421/104/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In September 2015, Richie and [[Jimmy Fallon]] covered the song in a humorous duet on ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon|The Tonight Show]]''. Within days, the clip had gone [[viral video|viral]], garnering over one million views on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/TV/2015/09/20/Jimmy-Fallons-Hello-duet-with-Lionel-Richies-head-goes-viral/1721442756615/ |last=Butler |first=Karen |website=[[United Press International]] |access-date=November 17, 2022 |date=September 20, 2015 |title=Jimmy Fallon's 'Hello' duet with Lionel Richie's head goes viral}}</ref>

sections.text:
A UK garage cover by Jhay Palmer featuring MC Image reached No. 69 on the UK Singles Chart and No. 11 on the UK Dance Singles Chart in 2002.

In September 2015, Richie and Jimmy Fallon covered the song in a humorous duet on The Tonight Show. Within days, the clip had gone viral, garnering over one million views on YouTube.

American singer Demi Lovato sang a rendition of the song as part of a tribute to Richie at the 58th Annual Grammy Awards on February 15, 2016. Her cover version eventually peaked at No. 15 on the Billboard Twitter Top Tracks chart.

Lea Michele and Jonathan Groff covered the song in Glee’s  episode "Hell-O”  in Glee season 1
